title: U.S. House · New Hampshire's 1st District
area: Eastern New Hampshire, including Manchester, Portsmouth and Rochester.

context.text: This is an open seat: incumbent Rep. Chris Pappas (D) did not seek re-election here and is instead the Democratic nominee for U.S. Senate. Stefany Shaheen, daughter of retiring Sen. Jeanne Shaheen, won the September 8, 2026 Democratic primary with 37.2% of the vote over Maura Sullivan (34.9%) and Carleigh Beriont (22.0%).

candidates.name: Stefany Shaheen
candidates.ballotNote: Won the September 8, 2026 Democratic primary with 37.2% of the vote in a nine-candidate field.
candidates.currentRole: Former Portsmouth, NH City Councilor and Chair of the Portsmouth Police Commission

priorities.text: Health care: says corporate monopolies and Wall Street investors have driven up health care costs, and says she supports Medicare for All and a public option while pursuing near-term steps such as breaking up health care monopolies and lowering prescription drug prices.

Affordability: opposes tariffs imposed by the Trump administration, saying they have raised costs for small businesses and consumers, and calls for refunding revenue collected from tariffs the Supreme Court found illegal.

Housing: says investor purchases of homes and tax breaks for hedge funds and private equity firms are driving up housing costs, and calls for ending those tax breaks and expanding support for first-time homebuyers.

positions.summary: Says she supports Medicare for All and a public option, and wants to break up health care corporate monopolies and let Medicare negotiate lower drug prices.
Calls for rolling back tariffs she describes as illegal and refunding the money they cost small businesses.
Calls for cutting red tape that prevents construction of new affordable housing and investing in the skilled trades to build homes faster.
Calls for overhauling ICE, including body cameras, a ban on masks, ending warrantless searches, and ending raids in schools, churches and hospitals.
Describes her own abortion care after a miscarriage and says she will fight for abortion access and reproductive rights.
positions.quote: You can know from my experience, exactly where I stand on abortion access and reproductive rights. I will always and tirelessly fight for both.

positions.summary: Calls for more local clean energy production and action to address climate change.
positions.quote: Increase local clean energy production: New Hampshire is already home to a number of solar, wind, hydro, and bio fuel companies. We need a lot more.

candidates.name: Anthony DiLorenzo

priorities.text: Lowering energy costs in New Hampshire.
priorities.quote: New Hampshire has some of the highest energy costs in the country. We have to fix that.

priorities.text: Balancing the federal budget through a constitutional amendment.
priorities.quote: Balance the federal budget by supporting a Balanced Budget Amendment to the U.S. Constitution.

priorities.text: Making healthcare more affordable and increasing access.
priorities.quote: Make healthcare more affordable and increase access.

positions.summary: In a May 2026 interview, said tariffs can generate revenue and encourage domestic manufacturing, while noting they only apply to foreign goods and favoring lower income taxes.
positions.quote: Tariffs can generate revenue, encourage domestic manufacturing and open markets for American products. Those are positive goals. At the same time, tax policy matters.

positions.summary: At a 2026 debate, said the remedy for illegal immigration is deportation and that he supports immigration enforcement.
positions.quote: I support law enforcement, including immigration enforcement, and the remedy again for illegal immigration is deportation.

candidates.researchNotes: Positions and statements come from his campaign issues page (a 21-point list with no detail), a 2026 Dartmouth interview, and debate remarks recorded by Citizens Count. He has not completed Ballotpedia's Candidate Connection survey and left most Citizens Count survey questions unanswered.

researchNotes: Basic-tier research. Sources: his campaign issues page, an April 29, 2026 interview with The Dartmouth, and a Citizens Count profile quoting a 2026 debate. Anthony DiLorenzo's campaign website returned no content when fetched, so his biography relies on news interviews and profiles and Ballotpedia. Shaheen's education and background details come from her campaign website; a third-party profile lists her degrees differently, so only the campaign's own description is used.
